questions.question: Concentration is defined as:
options: c = n/V — moles of solute divided by volume of solution in dm³
Mass divided by volume in cm³

questions.question: Before entering the formula, 200 cm³ must become:
The molar mass of Na2CO3 (Na 23, C 12, O 16) is:
10,6 g of Na2CO3 in 200 cm³ of solution gives a concentration of:

subtopics.title: Percentage Composition — the Compound's Mass Recipe

questions.question: The percentage of an element in a compound equals:
options: Its number of atoms divided by the total atoms
Its atomic number divided by the molar mass
The mass of that element in one mole, divided by the molar mass, times 100

questions.question: In ammonia, NH3 (M = 17), nitrogen's share is:
In methane, CH4 (M = 16), the four hydrogens together contribute:
The percentages of all elements in a compound must total:
options: 100 — and a different total announces an arithmetic error

subtopics.title: Empirical Formula — the Recipe Recovered from Percentages

questions.question: The 100 gram assumption is legitimate because:
options: A ratio does not care about sample size — 100 g just turns percentages into masses

questions.question: Masses must be converted to moles before forming the ratio because:
options: Formulas count atoms, and only moles count atoms — mass ratios mislead
Grams are too large a unit
The periodic table only lists moles

questions.question: For 52,2% C, 13,0% H, 34,8% O, dividing the mole values (4,35; 13,0; 2,175) by the smallest gives:
If the ratio step leaves a value of 1,5, you must:
options: Multiply the whole ratio by 2 — half atoms are not allowed

subtopics.title: Water of Crystallisation, the Full Method and the Traps

questions.question: Water of crystallisation is:
options: Water locked into a crystal's structure in a fixed ratio, like the ten H2O in Na2CO3·10H2O
Moisture on the outside of crystals
Water used to wash the crystals
The liquid the crystals dissolve into

questions.question: The molar mass of Na2CO3·10H2O is:
options: 286 g/mol — 106 for Na2CO3 plus 180 for ten waters

questions.question: The water's share of washing soda's mass is:
Leaving a volume in cm³ when computing concentration makes the answer:
In the cooldrink picture, a strong solution means:
options: Plenty of dissolved substance crowded into each litre

questions.question: Counting the packs first means:
options: Converting grams to moles before any division — 10,6 g of Na2CO3 is 0,1 mol

questions.question: Two jugs hold the same total concentrate but different volumes. Their concentrations are:
options: Different — concentration is about crowding, not totals

questions.question: The final concentration of the sodium carbonate solution is:
options: 0,5 mol per cubic decimetre — 0,1 mol in 0,2 dm³

questions.question: The empirical formula problem is 'reading the recipe backwards' because:
options: The formula is written right to left
You start from the finished compound's percentage label and reconstruct the atomic recipe
Recipes are always written in percentages

questions.question: With 100 g assumed, 13,0% hydrogen becomes:
options: 13,0 grams, which then converts to 13,0 moles by dividing by 1

questions.question: The recipe is simplified by:
options: Dividing every mole value by the smallest one

questions.question: The recovered recipe 2 : 6 : 1 for C, H and O is written:

subtopics.title: The Water Hiding in Dry Crystals

questions.question: The startling fact about washing soda crystals is that they are:
options: Nearly two-thirds water by mass, locked into the crystal structure

questions.question: Pricing the formula like an invoice means:
options: Estimating the shop price of the chemical
Reading the formula atom by atom, pricing each from the periodic table, and adding
Rounding every mass to the nearest ten

questions.question: The laboratory check of the 62,9% figure is:
options: Warming the crystals and confirming the mass loss matches the predicted share

questions.question: Subscripts in formulas like Na2CO3·10H2O are:
options: Multiplication instructions — skipping one poisons every later line
